active_paradigms.idea: Exact set-partitioning minimax solver using scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program is a demand-first greedy assignment followed by monotone best-improvement single moves and pairwise swaps. Its strength is that every accepted operation directly lowers the true maximum KVPR and swaps repair some packing conflicts, but it cannot cross a temporary worsening barrier and cannot perform multi-model exchanges. Replace the heuristic by a configuration set-partitioning formulation when the number of models is moderate. Deterministically enumerate every subset of models whose total model size is strictly below 80 GB; each subset is one feasible GPU configuration with a known load, residual memory, and fixed KVPR. Add one binary variable per configuration, require every model to occur in exactly one chosen configuration, and require exactly gpu_num configurations, including an empty configuration to represent unused GPUs. Encode minimax selection by also choosing one KVPR threshold from the sorted distinct configuration pressures, allowing only configurations at or below that chosen threshold, and minimize the selected threshold in one MILP call. This optimizes the evaluator's actual per-GPU ratio globally rather than optimizing a surrogate load balance. It is particularly valuable on instances where the greedy placement needs a 3-way or larger rearrangement to expose a lower-pressure packing.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimize the maximum of sum(req_rate/slo) divided by remaining GPU memory, which is the quantity whose cross-GPU maximum drives the reported score; feasibility and exact model coverage are hard constraints.
active_paradigms.cautions: Subset enumeration is exponential, so use it only when model count and feasible-subset count are modest, and use a deterministic cutoff/fallback for large instances. Do not include subsets with total size equal to 80 because they have zero residual memory and infinite KVPR; preserve the current program's strict fit convention. Configuration variables may select identical empty configurations multiple times, which is necessary when gpu_num exceeds the number of nonempty groups. Build threshold/configuration incidence constraints carefully so a selected configuration is forbidden whenever its fixed pressure exceeds the selected threshold.

active_paradigms.idea: Direct integer global search over assignments with scipy.optimize.differential_evolution
active_paradigms.description: Use SciPy's differential_evolution in its integer-variable mode to optimize a vector containing one GPU index for each model, with the objective evaluated directly from the induced placement. The current greedy-plus-local-search solution is an excellent deterministic seed because its weakness is not objective evaluation but its restricted one-move/one-swap neighborhood. Set bounds of [0, gpu_num-1] for every assignment coordinate and set integrality=True for all coordinates, then evaluate the exact maximum KVPR after grouping models by their candidate GPU. Return a very large finite penalty for any assignment having total size at least 80 GB on a GPU, rather than allowing division by zero or exceptions. Seed the initial population with the current greedy placement and several demand-balanced/random feasible assignments, while retaining differential evolution as the single direct optimization call. The solver can alter many model assignments simultaneously, so it can discover coordinated repackings that are inaccessible to monotonic local search. Use the final integer assignment itself as the placement, with no continuous relaxation or rounding stage.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The exact maximum final KVPR, with infeasible memory assignments made decisively worse than every feasible placement; this targets coordinated global reassignment rather than only local improvement.
active_paradigms.cautions: This is appropriate only if the installed SciPy supports differential_evolution's integrality argument; otherwise do not silently round continuous coordinates during objective evaluation because that creates large flat regions. Use a finite but safely dominant infeasibility penalty and explicitly reject residual memory <= 0. Runtime grows quickly with number of models, so cap popsize and maxiter based on evaluator limits and favor a seeded population. GPU labels are symmetric, so canonicalizing equivalent assignments in the objective cache can substantially reduce repeated work if caching is permitted.

active_paradigms.idea: Exact exhaustive assignment selection with itertools.product for small hidden instances
active_paradigms.description: For genuinely small cases, use itertools.product(range(gpu_num), repeat=len(models)) to enumerate every complete discrete placement and retain the feasible candidate with the smallest exact maximum KVPR. This is fundamentally different from the current method: it has no greedy ordering bias, no local-neighborhood restriction, and therefore certifies the global optimum for cases within its search budget. During each candidate evaluation, accumulate model sizes and weights per GPU, reject immediately if any used GPU has residual memory less than or equal to zero, and otherwise compute the same load/residual ratio as the evaluator. Empty GPUs contribute zero pressure, so they need no special balancing rule. A practical deterministic guard can select this method only when gpu_num ** len(models) is below a conservative operation budget; otherwise return the existing greedy-and-swap result. On distributions containing small but difficult combinatorial instances, exact enumeration can improve the average score disproportionately because it removes all heuristic error on those cases. Unlike a fractional flow or slot approximation, every retained candidate is a valid indivisible model placement and is scored by the true objective.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Obtain the globally minimal maximum KVPR on small instances, eliminating the current heuristic's failure modes from those evaluator cases while preserving exact memory feasibility.
active_paradigms.cautions: The search space is gpu_num to the power of model count, so the guard is essential; do not attempt this indiscriminately on large inputs. Evaluate using strict residual-memory positivity, not merely total size <= 80, to avoid infinite pressure. Symmetry can be reduced by fixing the first model on GPU 0 or by canonical GPU-label generation, but any pruning must not exclude feasible unlabeled partitions. Ensure the fallback remains deterministic and returns the required dictionary keyed by every GPU index.
